title: VPC node claim tracing and tiered retention controller for private residency
creator: Priya Patel
description: Implement a coordinated VPC 'node claim' tracing system plus a tiered retention controller that automates evidence packaging for private/VPC and on-prem deployments. This ticket covers: (1) a compact tamper-evident claim token emitted when a compute node attaches to a customer residency zone (VPC/on-prem); (2) distributed trace capture that ties requests to claim tokens and KV cache locality; (3) a retention controller that applies customer-configured retention tiers (hot/archival/legal-hold) and produces signed evidence bundles for audits and incident reports; and (4) gating rules that prevent automatic cross-region failover for nodes with active legal holds unless approved through an operator flow.
acceptance_criteria: Claim token produced on node provisioning and rotation; token includes node ID, region, attach_time, firmware/AMI digest and is signed by platform key
Requests and KV-cache events include claim token context and are retained for configured retention tier durations
Retention controller enforces three tiers (hot: 7d, warm: 90d, legal-hold: indefinite) configurable per-customer and emits signed evidence bundles when retention transitions occur
Failover orchestration refuses cross-region switchover for nodes with active legal-hold claim tokens unless an operator-approved override is recorded in the audit ledger
Evidence bundle exporter can push to customer-provided S3/GCS with KMS envelope-wrap and produces a verifiable manifest (SHA256 + signature)
End-to-end tests and a canary roll demonstrating retention transitions, evidence export, and blocked failover under legal-hold
tasks: Design claim token schema and signing workflow (security review required - referenced in comments)
Instrument runtime to attach claim token to request traces and KV cache events
Build retention controller microservice with pluggable backends (local ledger + customer bucket exporter)
Add failover gating: integrate with routing/orchestrator and operator-approval API
Create automated evidence exporter with KMS envelope option and manifest signer
Add observability: per-customer retention metrics, token rotation counts, export success/failure metrics
Write integration tests and run canary in staging private deployment

notes: Trade-offs: strict legal-hold enforcement increases blast radius for availability during region outages — design includes an operator approval workflow and an emergency 'juriswitch' path that records immutable justification. We prioritize provable evidence exports over transparent automatic failover in the presence of legal holds. Performance: token attach+trace adds minimal overhead; we will add batching to export manifests to reduce CPU overhead. Next steps: finalize HSM keyflow, add rotation CI tests, run staging canary with EU customer sandbox.
